  "text": "By morning Tobias had worn a pale place in the brim of his hat.

He sat in the church until the woman who cleaned it came with her bucket. She asked whether someone had died. He moved his knees to let her pass.

Outside, the gulls were back. A van stood at the bakery. Someone had dropped a glove beside the drain, and he picked it up and laid it on the wall, fingers pointing inland.

He took the road to Maren's house.

All eleven posts stood straight. The lantern lay beside the path. Its glass had not broken, and there was sand inside it, though the little door was fastened.

He left it where it lay.

At the porch he called her name. Then he knocked, using the side of his hand, as he always had when bringing fish.

The door opened under the knock.

Nothing had been overturned. Her father's rug lay square with the hearth. The lamp stood unlit on the sill, its chipped base turned toward the room. On the table was a cup with a little tea dried at the bottom.

Tobias went to the window.

From there he could see the beach, the path, his own footprints coming up it. The tide was out.

He stood a while with his hand on the lamp. The base was cold.

Before leaving, he carried the cup to the kitchen. He rinsed it and set it upside down beside the sink.

He could not bring himself to draw the curtains.",

  "text": "For three days Tobias took the longer road to the harbor.

On the fourth, rain came through a seam in his kitchen ceiling. He set a basin beneath it and went to find the ladder he had lent Maren in August.

It was behind her shed. One foot had sunk into the earth. He worked it loose, then stood with the ladder against his shoulder, looking at the house.

The curtains were still open.

He put the ladder down.

Inside, the air smelled of cold ashes and the apples she kept beneath the stairs. One had spoiled. He found it by touch, reaching among the sound ones, and carried it outside in his palm.

There was no good place to put it. At last he laid it under the hedge.

He went back for the cup. It had dried with a brown line near the handle that he had missed. He rubbed the mark with his thumb, then with the corner of a cloth. When it was clean, he set it upright in the cupboard.

The cupboard held five other cups. He had never noticed how many she owned.

Before he left, he checked the back door and shut the small window in the pantry. He did not touch the lamp.

Outside, he lifted the ladder. Its wet rung pressed against his neck.

At the gate he remembered the basin in his kitchen, how shallow it was, and hurried a little. Halfway home he stopped hurrying. The rain had ended. Water fell from the ladder onto his coat.",

  "text": "The basin had overflowed, but not by much. Tobias wiped the floor with an old shirt and left the basin where it was.

Next morning he climbed into the roof space. A slate had slipped near the chimney. Through the gap he could see a narrow piece of sky, lighter than he expected. He pushed a folded sack beneath the timbers and came down to make tea.

There were two apples in his coat pocket.

He had no recollection of taking them. He set them on the table, where they rocked a little before settling.

By noon he had bought a slate and borrowed a roofer's hammer. The repair took most of the afternoon. When he finished, he carried the ladder into his shed rather than leaving it against the wall.

There was room for it only if he moved the chair with the broken seat. Maren had brought the chair over in spring. He had promised to mend it before she had finished explaining what was wrong.

He turned it upside down on the bench.

The split ran along the grain. He found the glue, cleared its hardened mouth with a nail, and fitted the two edges together. One clamp was missing its wooden pad. He folded a scrap of cloth around the bare iron and tightened it carefully.

At supper he cut one apple into quarters. The other he put beneath the stairs, then brought it out again. It would keep well enough in the bowl.

Before bed he went to the shed and loosened the clamp a fraction. Glue had gathered along the join. He wiped it away while it was still soft.",
